evidence: Cic. Fam. 4.12.1: ibi M. Mārcellum … convēnī
Cic. Sen. 32: nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit
terms.comment: Transitive of meeting a person (aliquem convenīre); intransitive of people coming together in one place.

evidence: Cic. Att. 2.24.2: cum eō saepe congressus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With cum: to meet someone, usually to talk.

phrases.latin: itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus
phrases.english: so no one who wanted to see me has ever yet found me busy

phrases.latin: cum ab Epidaurō Pīraeum nāvī advectus essem, ibi M. Mārcellum, conlēgam nostrum, convēnī eumque diem ibi cōnsūmpsī, ut cum eō essem
phrases.english: when I had come by ship from Epidaurus to the Piraeus, I met our colleague Marcus Marcellus there, and spent the day there so as to be with him

sources: Lewis & Short: convenio · Lewis & Short: congredior
